## Findings
- claim-1: The basic ideal is \(J_v=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\); Grassmannian cohomology is \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) with Schur classes indexed by partitions in \((n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 197-218]
- claim-2: For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and the lower-adjoined Schur family generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- claim-3: In \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), multiplication is truncated Littlewood–Richardson multiplication over partitions in \(q^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269]
- claim-4: For the new specialization \[ (i,j,p,c)=(2,3,3,2),\quad q=i+p=5,\quad r=j+c=5, \] hence \(n=r+q=10\), \(t=r-j+1=3\), \(s=i+t-1=4\), and \(v=v_{5,4,3,10}\) is admissible.
- claim-5: With \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), the exact Schur-basis interval ideal is \[ J=J_v=\bigoplus_{\substack{(2,2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(5,5,5,5,5)}}\mathbb Z\,\bar s_\lambda . \]
- claim-6: For this specialization, \[ A_+=(\bar h_1,\bar h_2,\bar h_3,\bar h_4,\bar h_5). \]
- claim-7: In every degree \(d\), the complete lattice \((A_+J)_d\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of precisely the Pieri rows \[ \bar h_t\bar s_\lambda =\sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^5\\ \mu/\lambda\ {\rm horizontal}\ t\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\mu , \quad 1\le t\le5,\quad (2,2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^5,\quad |\lambda|=d-t. \]
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), \(p=q-i\), \(c=r-j\).  Take
\[
(i,j,p,c)=(2,3,3,2),
\quad q=5,\ r=5,\ n=10.
\]
Then
\[
t=r-j+1=3,\qquad s=i+t-1=4,
\]
so \(v=v_{5,4,3,10}\).  Explicitly,
\[
1\le3\le5,\quad 3\le4\le10,\quad 3>5+4-10=-1,
\]
hence this is admissible.

Put \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,5}\), and define the Grassmannian contraction
\[
J:=\iota^{-1}(J_v)\subseteq A,
\]
where \(\iota:H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{5,10})\hookrightarrow H^*(\mathrm{Fl}_{10})\) is the split inclusion.  The Schur basis of \(A\) is
\[
\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq5^5\}.
\]
[doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 197-218]

For \(\lambda=(\lambda _1,\ldots,\lambda _5)\subseteq5^5\), padded by zeroes, set
\[
I_\lambda=(1+\lambda _5,\,2+\lambda _4,\,\ldots,\,5+\lambda _1)
\]
and let \(u_\lambda\) be the permutation whose first five values are \(I_\lambda\) and whose final five values are the increasing complement.  Grassmannian Schubert classes satisfy
\[
\iota(\bar s_\lambda)=\sigma_{u_\lambda}.
\]
For \(\kappa,\lambda\subseteq5^5\), the Bruhat rank criterion gives
\[
u_\kappa\le u_\lambda
\iff I_{\kappa,a}\le I_{\lambda,a}\ (1\le a\le5)
\iff \kappa\subseteq\lambda.
\]
Indeed, if \(I_\kappa\le I_\lambda\) componentwise, then every northwest rank of \(u_\kappa\) is at least that of \(u_\lambda\): for the first \(x\le5\) positions this is immediate; for \(x=5+\ell\), the rank is
\[
M+\min(\ell,y-M),\qquad M=\#(I\cap[1,y]),
\]
which is increasing in \(M\). Conversely, if \(I_{\kappa,a}>I_{\lambda,a}\), the rank at \((a,I_{\lambda,a})\) violates the criterion.

Here
\[
u_{(2,2,2,0,0)}
=(1,2,5,6,7,3,4,8,9,10)=v_{5,4,3,10}.
\]
Since \(J_v=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\), intersection with the fixed-descent Grassmannian Schubert basis yields
\[
J=\bigoplus_{\substack{(2,2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(5,5,5,5,5)}}
\mathbb Z\,\bar s_\lambda.
\]
This is an integral direct sum because the displayed Schur classes are distinct members of the integral Schur basis.

Writing \(\bar h_t=\bar s_{(t)}\), \(\bar h_t=0\) for \(t>5\).  Since
\[
\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]
\]
and \(A_0=\mathbb Z\), every positive-degree class of \(A\) is a polynomial in
\(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5\) with zero constant term.  Therefore
\[
A_+=(\bar h_1,\bar h_2,\bar h_3,\bar h_4,\bar h_5).
\]

Consequently, in every partition-weight degree \(d\),
\[
(A_+J)_d=
\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\left\{
\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda:
1\le t\le5,\ 
(2,2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^5,\ 
|\lambda|=d-t
\right\}.
\]
Pieri and truncation give each displayed row exactly as
\[
\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda
=
\sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^5\\
\mu/\lambda\text{ a horizontal }t\text{-strip}}}
\bar s_\mu.
\]
Rows with no such \(\mu\) are the zero row and remain included.  If no \(\lambda\) has \(|\lambda|=d-t\), that row family is empty.  Thus these are the complete degreewise relation lattices, not merely sublattices.
